title: Review: Genes, the genetic code and genomes; HIV/AIDS and viral diseases; Gene regulation in prokaryotes (lac operon); Cell specialization, tissues, organs; Homeobox genes and development
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: IM06#t3 term and clue written for the game; GE03#t3 term and clue written for the game; GR02#t2 term and clue written for the game; GE03#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE07a#N.5b, GE03#N.9b, GR02#N.4, GR04#N.3, IM06#N.15b, CE07a#N.3b, GE03#N.5b, GR02#N.9, CE07a#N.11. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Envelope
items.clue: Lipid bilayer around the particle, taken from the host cell membrane.

items.label: Stop codon
items.clue: UAA, UAG or UGA: specifies no amino acid, so the polypeptide ends there.

items.label: Promoter
items.clue: Site where RNA polymerase binds before transcribing the structural genes.

items.label: Degenerate code
items.clue: Feature meaning that most amino acids are specified by more than one triplet.

questions.stem: During development of a hypothetical species of fly, a signal induces expression of gene A in certain cells. Protein A is a transcription factor that activates gene B, and protein B is a transcription factor that activates gene C. In a mutant fly, gene B is deleted. Which proteins are predicted to be made in the mutant's cells that normally make all three proteins?

options.text: Protein A only, because gene C needs protein B in order to be switched on
Proteins A and C, because gene C switches on at its own set time in development
None of the three proteins, because losing gene B shuts down the whole pathway
All three proteins, because the cell makes protein B from another gene when needed

questions.stem: In human mitochondria, the codon UGA codes for the amino acid tryptophan, whereas in the cytoplasm of most organisms it is a stop codon. How does this finding affect the claim that the genetic code is evidence of common ancestry?

options.text: It shows that each kind of organism evolved its own code, so the code is not evidence of common ancestry.
It proves that common ancestry is false, because one exception is enough to disprove a shared code.
It does not undermine the claim: the code is nearly universal, and rare variants arose later.
It shows the code is fixed by chemistry, since mitochondria still use exactly the same code.

questions.stem: Escherichia coli bacteria growing in a medium without lactose are transferred to a medium containing lactose. Within minutes they begin to synthesise beta-galactosidase, the enzyme that hydrolyses lactose. What causes this change in gene expression?

options.text: Lactose is the raw material from which the bacteria build the new enzyme
Lactose acts as a transcription factor, binding directly to the gene's promoter
Lactose stops the bacteria from transcribing the gene coding for the repressor
Lactose binds to the repressor protein, which releases the operator

questions.explanation: Lactose (as its isomer allolactose) binds to the lac repressor and changes its shape so that it no longer binds the operator. RNA polymerase can then transcribe the genes.

questions.stem: Female fruit flies with extra copies of the bicoid gene lay eggs containing more Bicoid mRNA than normal at the head end. What is predicted for their embryos?

options.text: The head region extends further towards the tail end than normal.
No change, because each cell's fate was fixed at fertilisation and Bicoid only marks the region.
No change, because Bicoid is an on/off switch and the head-end cells receive it anyway.
Cells near the tail end lose their head genes, because they receive too little Bicoid.

questions.explanation: More Bicoid means the threshold concentrations for head genes are reached further along the embryo, so head structures form over a longer stretch.

questions.stem: A drug stops retroviral DNA from being inserted into the host genome. Reverse transcriptase still works. Cells treated with the drug are exposed to a retrovirus. Which result is predicted?

options.text: No viral DNA is made, so the viral RNA stays in the cytoplasm.
Viral DNA is made, but it is not integrated, so new viral progeny are not produced.
Viral proteins are still made, because ribosomes translate the viral RNA genome directly.
The cells stop transcribing their own genes, because their genome has been blocked.

questions.explanation: Viral DNA forms but cannot join the host genome, so it is not transcribed and translated to make new viruses.

questions.stem: A person's skin cells and liver cells have very different structures and functions. Which statement best explains how these differences arise?

options.text: Each cell type keeps the genes it uses and has lost the genes that it does not use.
The genes in each cell type have mutated to suit the jobs that the cell needs to do.
The two cell types express different combinations of genes, at different levels.
Both cell types express all of their genes, but their surroundings shape them.

questions.explanation: The phenotype of a cell is determined by the combination of genes that are expressed and the levels at which they are expressed.

questions.stem: Which statement about the genetic code is correct?

options.text: A single codon can code for several different amino acids.
Many amino acids are each specified by more than one codon.
Each species uses its own codons for the amino acids.
The start codon AUG is a start signal that codes for no amino acid.

questions.explanation: For example, several codons code for glycine, while each codon specifies one amino acid or a stop signal.

questions.stem: A mutant strain of E. coli makes a lac repressor that still binds the operator normally, but can no longer bind lactose. What happens when these bacteria are given lactose?

options.text: The enzymes are made as normal, because lactose can still bind the operator and switch the genes on.
The enzymes are not made, because the repressor stays on the operator even with lactose present.
The enzymes are made when lactose is present, but they have altered amino acid sequences.
The enzymes are made, because lactose stops the bacteria transcribing the repressor gene.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, leaf cells make large amounts of a protein that binds chlorophyll, but the root cells of the same plant make none of it. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: In root cells, the base sequence of the gene has been changed, and the gene no longer codes for the protein.
Both cell types carry the gene for the protein, but it is expressed in leaf cells and not in root cells.
Root cells have lost the gene for the protein from their DNA because they did not use it.
Root cells do not need the protein, so they choose not to make it, unlike the cells of leaves.
